one_line: The scope is a direct match for our restroom trailer line and our Denver and USCG work, but we can't commit until we confirm whether our MBE status qualifies for this Texas "MBE" set-aside, whether we have a two-stall unit that meets the specs, and whether we can afford bi-weekly servicing in Livingston, TX from California. The actual solicitation documents are not in the bid pack.
scope: Texas DPS wants a contractor to supply, install, and maintain one two-stall non-ADA mobile restroom facility at DPS Livingston (3161 US-59, Livingston, TX 77351). The unit needs 110V/20A power, heating and cooling, a 125-gal onboard (or hose-fed) water supply, a 300-gal external tank with auxiliary pump, a 350-gal onboard wastewater tank, a female stall (sink and toilet), and a male stall (sink, toilet, and urinal). The contractor must service it bi-weekly: refill water, pump out waste per state regulations, disinfect, and clean floors. Service runs from award through August 31, 2027, with four optional one-year renewals.
fit: Core competency: 'Man Camp & Temporary Housing' and 'Facility Support & Utilities' cover restrooms, portable sanitation, water delivery, and waste removal. Our fleet includes shower and restroom facilities.

Directly relevant past performance: City and County of Denver SC-00011558 (Aug 2026 – ongoing, multi-year), where we provide, deliver, and service climate-controlled restroom trailers with pump-outs, cleaning, supplies, and maintenance. Value printed as ~$100,00.00 [CONFIRM: amount].
USCG 70Z02826FMIAM0008 ($78,500, May–Jul 2026): restroom/shower trailers with water and wastewater support, maintenance, and demobilization.

Our standard operation already includes recurring servicing (water resupply, RCRA-compliant gray/black water removal, sanitizing, consumables), a 24/7 emergency line, and weekly QC reports. Bi-weekly is less often than our standard weekly service.
Our restroom trailers come with independent HVAC, on-demand hot water, and sealed gray/black tanks, which line up with the HVAC, hot/cold water, and holding-tank requirements.
The set-aside is labeled MBE and our profile lists MBE status (subject to the eligibility check under gaps).
Work area is nationwide, and the estimated value ($100,000) is in line with our past contract sizes.
red_flags: Set-aside eligibility is unclear. HigherGov tags this as MBE, but the solicitation refers to Texas HUBs (Historically Underutilized Businesses) and a HUB Subcontracting Plan. Our profile lists SBE and MBE but no Texas HUB certification, and it doesn't say who certified our MBE status.
No solicitation documents: the bid pack has 0 attachments. All requirements come from HigherGov's description and AI summary, not the Texas DPS solicitation itself.

Unit match is unproven. The price list has no two-stall restroom-only trailer. The closest rows are the 13ft 3-stall and 22ft 6-stall Luxury Shower-Restroom Combination Trailers. The spec calls for exactly two stalls (one with a urinal), a 350-gal onboard waste tank, and a 300-gal external tank with auxiliary pump.

Servicing logistics: the work is bi-weekly at one site in Livingston, TX, and we're based in Marina del Rey, CA. Unless we have a local service partner or depot, travel cost could wipe out the margin on a single-unit contract.
Waste must be pumped 'according to state regulations'. Our profile lists no Texas licenses or permits for hauling or disposing of wastewater.
NAICS 562991 and PSC S208 are not among our listed codes. This matters less on a state (SLED) bid, but it shows the agency sees this as septic/portable-toilet service work.
Evidence of financial stability must be provided on request.
The deadline (2026-11-27) is the day after Thanksgiving and leaves 13 days. The submission time and time zone aren't given.
competition: No incumbent is identified. HigherGov found no past awards by Texas DPS under NAICS 562991. The NAICS 562991 + PSC S208 benchmarks are federal awards with 1–8 offers each, mostly from local portable-toilet, septic, and plumbing firms (for example Navo & Sons, Brave Eagle, A-1 Portajohns, Miller and Company). That suggests local Texas sanitation vendors are the likely competition. [CONFIRM: incumbent at DPS Livingston, if any]
price_signal: The agency estimates $100,000. The pack doesn't say whether that covers only the initial period or includes the renewals. The benchmarks are weak comparisons (mostly porta-johns and septic pumping): Brave Eagle latrines $80,662 (about 3 months, 4 offers), Navo & Sons septic pumping $64,609 (multi-year), A-1 Portajohns $10,512 (about 13 months). Our own references: the Denver restroom trailer contract is printed as ~$100,00.00 [CONFIRM], and our USCG template priced a restroom/shower trailer at $8,995/unit for a 30-day job. On the price list, the 13ft 3-stall Luxury Shower-Restroom trailer is $3,995 (15 days–1 month) and $2,495–3,995 (more than 3 months), but the billing basis is unspecified and there's no two-stall row. [CONFIRM: monthly unit rate, bi-weekly service rate, delivery/setup/pickup for Livingston, TX]
